title: Senior Staff Software Engineer-Voice AI Agent Prompting
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Forward Deployed Engineer, Voice AI Agent Engineering designs, builds, ships, and operates voice AI agents whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret caller intent over a live audio channel, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the caller's behalf. The engineer works across the full lifecycle: shaping ambiguous call flows and telephony requirements into precise specifications, authoring the instructions and prompts that govern voice agent behavior, proving through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly on real calls. This is not a machine learning or AI research role — the engineer does not train foundation or speech models — but it is distinct from traditional software engineering, where systems follow deterministic call-flow logic rather than selecting execution paths at runtime. 

Two things follow, and voice makes both harder. First, the agent's most important logic often lives in natural language — instructions, prompts, tool descriptions, and guardrails — which must be engineered, versioned, and reviewed with the same discipline as code, while also holding up under what a spoken channel adds: turn-taking, barge-in, and disambiguating what speech recognition got wrong. Second, because behavior is probabilistic and happens live on a call, correctness is established by measuring behavior at scale — including latency, containment, and transcription accuracy — rather than by asserting fixed outputs, making automated evaluation a first-class engineering activity rather than a quality-assurance afterthought. The engineer owns the correctness of what ships to a live caller, whether a human or an agent produced it. 

What You Get to Do in This Role: 

  • Build voice AI agents. Design and ship agentic voice applications — intent interpretation, multi-step reasoning, tool invocation, and action on the caller's behalf — together with the CTI, CCaaS, and telephony integrations that make them usable in production. 

  • Design AI-driven autonomous voice workflows. Decompose call flows and business processes into the steps and decision points a voice agent can execute — determining where autonomy is appropriate, where a live-agent handoff is required, and how misrecognition, retries, and escalation are handled. 

  • Engineer for what voice demands. Build experiences that hold context across turns, manage barge-in and interruption, recover gracefully from speech-recognition error, disambiguate caller intent, and confirm before consequential actions — all within the latency budget a live call imposes. 

  • Author and maintain voice agent instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern voice agent behavior — as engineering artifacts under review and regression coverage, not configuration text. 

  • Engineer prompts for reliability rather than demo quality. Iterate prompts against measured call outcomes: task decomposition, golden call transcripts, structured output schemas, grounding and citation, graceful hand-back to a human agent, and the token and latency cost that directly shapes caller experience. 

  • Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic voice behavior. Design and operate the evaluation that makes change safe on a live channel — golden call datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring calibrated to human QA review, CI gates, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, grounding, and tool-selection testing specific to voice. 

  • Specify precisely and direct AI coding agents. Convert customer call-flow and telephony requirements into testable specifications with explicit scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria; decompose work into agent-sized tasks; and review agent output for correctness and maintainability. You own the result regardless of what produced it. 

  • Deliver as a forward deployed engineer, embedded in the voice stack. Work directly inside a customer's telephony, CTI, and CCaaS environment — building against their call data, integrations, and channels, tuning instructions and evaluation sets against live traffic, and returning with evidence that improves the product. 

  • Own quality, safety, and reliability on live calls. Monitor call containment, hallucination, unsafe actions, and transcription accuracy; defend against prompt injection and data leakage on live calls; and feed production call failures back into specifications and evaluation sets. 

  • Collaborate across product, design, and engineering. Partner with product managers, designers and platform teams to define success criteria, align on tradeoffs, and communicate capability and risk clearly

Qualifications

To Be Successful in This Role:

A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production voice applications, including hands-on delivery of AI-native voice agent features that real callers depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts for voice, designing AI-driven autonomous call workflows, and building the evaluation and testing that verifies them against live call traffic, is required. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity, embedded in their voice and contact center environment, is required. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers.  

Education:Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degrees or certifications are a plus but are not a substitute for a demonstrated record of shipping reliable, production voice AI agents. 

Key Competencies, Skills, and Experience 

  • Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing. 

  • AI native voice application development. Hands-on experience building applications where model-driven behavior is central — agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling the latency, cost, and failure modes unique to a live audio channel. 

  • AI-driven autonomous workflow design. Demonstrated experience designing workflows in which voice agents carry out multi-step call processes with limited supervision: call-flow decomposition, decision points and autonomy boundaries, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, exception and retry handling, and observability over what the agent did and why. 

  • Voice and telephony platform expertise. Practical experience with telephony integration, speech recognition and synthesis, and streaming audio — including the barge-in, turn-taking, and confirmation patterns a live call requires. 

  • Agentic instruction authoring. Demonstrated skill writing and maintaining the natural-language logic that governs voice agent behavior — instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and refusal and escalation rules — with versioning, review, and regression coverage applied as they would be to code. 

  • Prompt engineering. Intent-driven prompt design tuned for voice: decomposition, golden and few-shot examples, structured output and schema enforcement, grounding and citation, and disciplined iteration against call-level evaluation results rather than impressions. 

  • Evaluation and testing of non-deterministic voice systems. Ability to build measurable frameworks assessing call quality, agent behavior, tool-selection accuracy, and regression risk — golden call datasets, scenario suites, model-as-judge scoring with human QA calibration, continuous evaluation pipelines, and drift detection — plus adversarial, jailbreak, and grounding testing. 

  • Specification precision and architectural judgment. Ability to define call-flow problems rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements them correctly, and to decide soundly when to solve a problem in code, in instructions, or by delegating to an agent. 

  • Safety, security, and data handling. Working knowledge of risks specific to AI-integrated voice applications — prompt injection, sensitive-data and call-recording leakage, over-broad tool access, unsafe autonomous action — translated into concrete guardrails, least-privilege controls, and monitoring. 

  • Forward deployed delivery and stakeholder communication. Comfort working directly with customers inside their telephony environment under incomplete information and fixed timelines, judgment about when a fast local solution is right and when to hold out for the durable one, and credibility communicating capability, limitation, and risk to non-engineers. 

Desired Experience:

  • Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment. 

  • Voice and contact center technology. Telephony and contact center platforms, IVR, speech recognition and synthesis, streaming audio, and real-time latency optimization. 

  • Conversation design partnership. Experience working alongside conversation or content designers, contributing to dialogue flow, tone, and error-recovery design. 

  • Evaluation and observability tooling. Evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production call transcripts at scale. 

  • Enterprise domain depth. Customer service, contact center operations, sales, or enterprise workflow, at a depth sufficient to challenge a requirement rather than only implement it. 

  • Years of Experience. At least 10 years of experience in software engineering with at least 2 years of experience in deploying contemporary AI solutions at customers

Job Description

About the team

The Conversational AI team at ServiceNow builds the core platform behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI experience. We are a group of applied scientists and software engineers working at the intersection of research and production. Our work spans the full stack that makes Otto capable: agent orchestration, including harness engineering, prompt tuning, agent skills, policy design, and quality evaluation across languages; the A2A and MCP protocols that let agents collaborate and connect to tools; background channels and conversational triggers that bring agents into action; AI-native licensing and pricing; and the central caching layer that connects the ServiceNow platform to the services powering Otto.

We are seeking a Staff AI-Native DevOps Engineer to join a new DevOps practice within the Conversational AI team. You will own the build, deployment, and reliability of the systems behind ServiceNow Otto, our conversational AI platform, from commit through production across our SaaS environments. Your work will span CI/CD pipelines, release automation, infrastructure on Kubernetes, observability, and the operational tooling that lets agent orchestration, MCP and A2A services, and the central caching layer ship safely and frequently. You will partner closely with applied scientists and software engineers to make AI-native delivery repeatable, measurable, and secure. This role combines deep expertise in cloud infrastructure, containerization, orchestration, and infrastructure as code with a practical understanding of how ML and LLM-based services behave in production, and a bias toward pragmatic engineering with measurable impact on deployment velocity and service reliability.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • Deep expertise in designing, building, and operating scalable, reliable, and secure cloud-native applications and infrastructure.
  • Strong software engineering skills, with experience developing infrastructure tooling and automation using Go, Python, or similar languages.
  • Experience leading complex infrastructure initiatives, establishing engineering best practices, and driving adoption across multiple teams.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose complex distributed systems issues and drive improvements in performance, reliability, and operational efficiency.
  • Strong understanding of modern AI technologies, including Large Language Models (LLMs), Generative AI, and agentic architectures, with the ability to apply these concepts to engineering and operational challenges.
  • An AI-native engineering mindset, proactively leveraging AI tools and automation to accelerate development, improve operational efficiency, and deliver more intelligent, resilient systems.

DevOps:

  • Deploy, scale, and operate distributed microservices in production Kubernetes environments, including managing application lifecycle, networking, security, and service reliability.
  • Design and implement infrastructure automation using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and Kubernetes-native tooling, including Terraform, Ansible, Helm, and Kubernetes Operators.
  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows using tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Tekton, and ArgoCD to automate testing, deployment, and release management.
  • Implement observability, monitoring, and incident response practices, performing root cause analysis and driving remediation to improve availability, fault tolerance, and operational resilience.
  • Architect and optimize cloud infrastructure across public and private cloud environments, with an emphasis on security, scalability, cost efficiency, and operational simplicity.

AI skills:

Artificial intelligence strategy is a critical skill at your level — it applies to how you build and to what you build. 

  • Confident use of AI coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot or Cursor, paired with the critical eye to review AI-generated code as rigorously as any other — catching logic errors, security anti-patterns, and missed edge cases rather than treating model output as production-ready. 
  • AI-assisted debugging and trace analysis, and a clear understanding of the data privacy rules governing what goes into a prompt.
  • Understanding of LLM-powered application architectures, including model inference, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool calling, and agentic workflows, with an awareness of their infrastructure, scalability, and reliability implications.
  • Ability to deploy, operate, and troubleshoot AI-powered services in production, including managing model API integrations, observability, latency, resource utilization, and operational costs.

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or related experience.
  • 6+ years of experience deploying and operating containerized applications and distributed services in production environments. 
  • 4+ years of hands-on experience with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, and infrastructure automation.
  • Proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language, such as Go, Python, or Bash, with experience building production-grade automation and tooling.
  • Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools in software engineering workflows, with demonstrated ability to validate, debug, and safely integrate AI-generated code.
  • Working knowledge of LLMs, Generative AI, and agentic AI concepts, including their integration patterns and operational considerations.

Preferred requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in software engineering, infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or platform engineering.
  • Extensive experience architecting and operating Kubernetes-based SaaS platforms at scale, including multi-service deployments and complex production environments.
  • Experience developing Kubernetes Operators, custom controllers, or other Kubernetes-native automation to manage application lifecycle and infrastructure operations.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership in driving cross-team infrastructure initiatives, improving production reliability, and establishing scalable platform engineering practices.
  • Hands-on experience deploying, integrating, or operating LLM-powered applications or agentic systems in production environments. Experience building AI-enabled infrastructure automation, observability, incident diagnosis, or remediation workflows to improve platform reliability and engineering productivity.

title: Senior Reliability Engineer - Veza
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the pioneer in identity security, purpose-built to answer the fundamental question enterprises face: who can and should take what action on what data. Veza's Access Graph platform maps an organization's entire identity ecosystem across users, groups, roles, policies, permissions, and resources—providing deep visibility and control over human, non-human, and agentic identities across SaaS, cloud, on-prem, and custom applications. With over 30 billion access permissions under management, global enterprises including Blackstone, Expedia, and Wynn Resorts trust Veza to manage privileged access monitoring, non-human identity security, access entitlement management, and next-generation identity governance.

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, Veza is now part of the ServiceNow family, with the acquisition closing in March 2026. The combination brings together Veza's AI-native Access Graph with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and agentic workflows, enabling organizations to enforce end-to-end identity security rooted in the principle of least privilege across applications, data, cloud environments, and AI agents. For engineers joining Veza today, this means the scale and resources of an enterprise platform company, with the product velocity and mission-driven focus of a security innovator at a pivotal moment in the industry.

  • Strong understanding of cybersecurity concepts, identity and access, governance and risk, and security operations. 
  • Required strong working knowledge of enterprise networking concepts, including routing, switching, VLANs, subnetting, firewalls, DNS, NAT, and network segmentation. 
  • Familiarity with capturing network traffic via SPAN ports, port mirroring, TAPs, packet capture brokers, NetFlow, and network telemetry. 
  • Ability to understand and explain how security platforms integrate with customer network environments to collect data, provide visibility, and support technical validation during demos, POVs, and POCs. 
  • Strong presentation, storytelling, and executive communication skills. 
  • Ability to engage effectively with technical practitioners, business stakeholders, and executive buyers. 
  • Demonstrated track record of contributing to technical wins, deal progression, and successful customer outcomes. 
  • BS degree in Computer Science, MIS, Cybersecurity, or equivalent experience. 

Preferred Experience

  • Background in Security Operations or security engineering 
  • Experience with asset discovery across IoT, OT, or IoMT environments 
  • Exposure to vulnerability management or risk-based vulnerability programs

  • 3+ years of experience supporting Process Mining, process optimisation, value realisation, operational discovery, or process improvement programmes with enterprise customers

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The role 

This senior principal solution architect is a functional and technical expert who consults with customers on implementing ServiceNow’s Security and Risk solutions in line with leading practices, accelerating customer business outcomes and helping build the practice. The role is laser-focused on the most relevant customer challenges. It supports sales cycles, engages directly with customers and partners, and advocates for customer needs within ServiceNow (Product Management, Customer & Partner Excellence, Training & Certification). 

The solution architect brings architectural guidance, industry business acumen, deep product expertise, innovation, and knowledge capital to customers and partners. 

Responsibilities 

  • Lead pre-sales activities: sales presentations, solutioning and scoping workshops, SOW development with clear deliverables and effort estimates, scope definition and change order triggers, and engagement sizing with Services Account Executives and Sales team members. 
  • Serve as a lead member of the engagement team, focused on connecting Security and Risk workflow applications to the customer’s technology landscape while advising on governance leading practices. 
  • Engage senior leadership, including CXOs, on implementation roadmap and change management. 
  • Partner with the Platform Architect team to surface proactive platform risks in customer landscapes. 
  • Act as practice director on marquee accounts for Security and Risk, leading delivery teams, providing oversight and technical expertise, and owning adherence to delivery standards. 
  • Design and deliver Security and Risk solutions with a technical architecture built for long-term success, following ServiceNow technical standards and leading practices. 
  • Design solutions for common customer use cases and publish them (to Solution Consultants, Customer Community, and others) for broader consumption. 
  • Build mutually beneficial relationships with Security and Risk product owners and stakeholders to promote awareness of capabilities and roadmaps. 
  • Lead office hours, presentations, webinars, and learning events for field delivery stakeholders (advisory, delivery, GTM) showcasing customer use cases and successes. 
  • Drive continuous improvement of delivery and engagement materials with the Customer & Partner Excellence team. 
  • Enable and mentor the ServiceNow delivery team and partner ecosystem. 
  • Create documentation and service offerings that promote our services. 
  • Flex across other areas of Risk and Security to maintain utilization KPIs. 
  • Travel up to 20% annually, driven by customer needs and internal meetings. 

Qualifications

To be successful in this role, we need someone who has: 

  • 12+ years in a professional services organization, or equivalent education and experience. 
  • 8+ years of consulting and/or configuration experience implementing complex technologies, including integrations and portals. 
  • 5+ years implementing ServiceNow Security and Risk solutions. 
  • Strong experience with TPRM, USEM, VR, SIR, IRM (RC, TPRM, BCM), OpsRes, and AI Control Tower. 
  • Strong understanding of the risk and security regulatory landscape and standards such as FFIEC, DORA, OpsRes, SEC, OCC, and SOX. 
  • Working knowledge of NIST CSF and other industry-specific frameworks. 
  • Experience with cross-functional domains such as asset management, service management, CMDB, and Risk and Security, including ITOM modules (Event Management, Discovery, CMDB, Service Graph Connectors). 
  • Strong understanding of Now Assist, RaptorDB, and Vault ZTA. 
  • Experience with cross-functional solutions and architectural foundations in large, heavily regulated enterprises such as FSI and HCLS. 
  • Experience applying AI to work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving: AI-powered tools, workflow automation, AI-driven insights, or the impact of AI on the function or industry. 
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and consult senior leaders in a matrixed organization (identifying needs, presenting options with pros, cons, and risks) and to provide thought leadership to sponsors and stakeholders. 
  • Customer-centric mindset, willing to go the extra mile and break down barriers to customer success. 
  • Ability to work with technical and non-technical customers, gather requirements, analyze information, and design comprehensive solutions. 
  • Ability to produce visually rich conceptual design documents for audiences of varying business and technical aptitude. 
  • Experience running solution presentations and securing customer acceptance of solution designs.

Relationship Management & Strategic Partnership

As a strategic thought partner to executive level GTM Sales leaders, this HR Business Partner Director translates business goals into people strategy across talent, leadership development, organization design, and culture. You will own the people strategy, functional people plan, and you will bring data and foresight to people decisions related to growth, productivity, and margin. You will also be the voice of the business within HR, aligning HRBP, COE, and shared services partners to deliver fit-for-purpose solutions for a matrixed, AI-native sales organization.

What You’ll Do

  • Shape and lead the functional people strategy, linking talent, leadership, and culture priorities to the business plan.

  • Lead strategic workforce planning, including headcount, spans and layers, and role design, so the organization grows efficiently within planned investment.

  • Anticipate people risks, such as attrition in critical roles, change fatigue, and capability gaps, and build mitigation and contingency plans before they affect performance.

  • 10+ years of experience in senior HR business partnering or equivalent, including direct executive client support, management coaching, and team development.
  • Experience in a technology or SaaS business, ideally supporting a sales or go-to-market organization.
  • Hands-on experience applying AI in HR or business work, such as using AI tools, automating workflows, or interpreting AI-driven insights to improve decisions.

descriptionHtml:

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Position Overview:

The Executive Assistant is a force multiplier and operational partner to the Senior Executive Assistant, supporting the executive office of the President and Chief Financial Officer. This role focuses on event execution, communications support, administrative operations, and after-hours backup. The Executive Assistant reports to the Senior Executive Assistant and works under their strategic direction on all complex or executive-facing decisions. 

The Sr. EA retains ownership of calendar management, strategic cross-functional coordination, executive communications strategy, and complex vendor relationships. The Executive Assistant amplifies the Sr. EA's capacity by owning execution on defined operational areas. 

Key Responsibilities:

Event Coordination & Logistics: 

  • Execute event planning and logistics under Sr. EA strategic direction, including departmental meetings, executive office events, and organization-wide initiatives (e.g., holiday parties, town halls, all-hands meetings) 
  • Manage vendor coordination, catering, transportation, and on-site setup 
  • Track RSVPs, attendee confirmations, and special accommodations 
  • Ensure all prep materials for upcoming meetings are available and accounted for; track meeting attendees and flag status to Sr. EA to determine next steps 
  • Ensure materials and run-of-show documents are available to President and CFO 
  • Handle post-event follow-up and execute event troubleshooting and real-time problem-solving 

Communications Support & Coordination:

  • Under the Sr EA guidance, the EA role will: 
  • Manage routine email processing, routing, and responses 
  • Coordinate scheduling emails, meeting confirmations, and calendar updates 
  • Maintain communication logs and prepare executive communication summaries 

Calendar & Scheduling Support:

  • Maintain calendar accuracy and update logistics for confirmed meetings 
  • Monitor the calendar for conflicts and flag to Sr. EA immediately 
  • Prepare weekly calendar reviews and highlight key activities for Sr. EA 
  • Coordinate with external participants on scheduling logistics 
  • Support scheduling calls and meeting coordination under Sr. EA direction 

Administrative Operations & Support: 

  • Maintain OCFO filing systems, databases, and operational documentation 
  • Prepare executive materials: reports, presentations, briefing documents 
  • Handle office management and supply ordering 
  • Process expenses, reimbursements, and financial documentation 
  • Manage shared calendars, scheduling tools, and software administration 

Cross-Functional Coordination: 

  • Execute multi-executive scheduling logistics under Sr. EA strategy 
  • Set up meetings and coordinate follow-up on Sr. EA direction 
  • Manage operational details with internal stakeholders 
  • Document meetings, action items, and deliverables 
  • Serve as escalation point for operational issues 

Team Operations & Knowledge Management:

  • Assist with EA team scheduling and coordination 
  • Update and maintain EA playbooks and operational documentation 
  • Support onboarding and knowledge transfer procedures 
  • Maintain shared team resources and calendars 
  • Document processes and operational best practices 

After-Hours & Urgent Support:

  • Handle urgent after-hours requests and escalate appropriately 
  • Maintain communication during business-critical situations 
  • Escalate all executive-facing decisions to Sr. EA 

Reporting & Authority:

Reports to: Senior Executive Assistant 

Authority Level: Operational execution on defined responsibilities under Sr. EA direction. Does not own calendar strategy, executive communications strategy, or cross-functional coordination strategy. All executive-facing or strategic decisions escalate to Sr. EA.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications & Competencies:

  • 5+ years as an Executive assistant
  • This position will require trips to the Bay Area
  • Social media skills, including creating and managing content across platforms
  • Strong organizational and project management skills; ability to manage multiple priorities 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; professional correspondence ability 
  • Ability to work independently and follow Sr. EA direction without constant oversight 
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in documentation and logistics 
  • Ability to remain calm and problem-solve in high-pressure environments 
  • Proficiency with Outlook, Teams, Office 365, and calendar management software 
  • Demonstrated ability to follow processes and escalate appropriately 
  • Flexible, adaptable, and willing to adjust priorities as needed 
  • Discretion and professionalism in handling confidential information 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting C-suite or senior executive team 
  • Event planning and coordination experience 
  • Experience with vendor management and contract coordination 
  • Knowledge of financial operations or compliance requirements 
  • Experience working as part of a larger administrative team 

What Success Looks Like:

  • Sr. EA can delegate event execution without micromanaging logistics 
  • Routine communications are handled professionally without Sr. EA involvement 
  • Executive-facing communications always go through Sr. EA before delivery 
  • Calendar logistics are executed perfectly; Sr. EA owns the calendar strategy 
  • Urgent after-hours issues are handled competently or escalated immediately 
  • Sr. EA has more bandwidth for strategic work due to execution support 
  • No duplicate effort or parallel decision-making between Executive Assistant and Sr. EA 

Work Environment & Expectations:

  • Fast-paced environment with competing priorities and time-sensitive requests 
  • Occasional after-hours support for urgent executive needs 
  • Collaboration with Sr. EA, finance teams, compliance, and cross-functional partners 
  • High level of professionalism and confidentiality required 
  • Flexibility and adaptability to changing circumstances and priorities 
  • Support role—all executive decisions and strategy owned by Sr. EA 

Key Distinctions: This Role vs. Senior Executive Assistant:

Executive Assistant OWNS: 

  • Event execution and vendor logistics 
  • Routine communications and scheduling 
  • Administrative operations and documentation 
  • After-hours urgent support 

Senior Executive Assistant OWNS: 

  • Calendar strategy and all hold decisions 
  • Executive communications strategy and messaging 
  • Cross-functional coordination and stakeholder relationships 
  • Compliance and governance decisions 
  • Strategic project coordination 
  • All executive-facing interactions and decisions 
  • Supervision and direction of Executive Assistant role 
  • Travel logistics coordination (managed through external Travel Manager)

  • Proven experience operating stateful and distributed workloads on Kubernetes, including databases, data services, or other mission-critical platform components.

  • Experience owning complex technical initiatives end-to-end, from architecture and design through implementation, deployment, and operational support.
  • Hands-on experience with containers, CI/CD, GitOps practices, and Infrastructure-as-Code using tools such as Terraform, Crossplane, or equivalent technologies.
  • Experience implementing observability and reliability best practices, including metrics, logging, tracing, monitoring, alerting, and service-level objectives.
  • Proven ability to drive technical strategy through architectural design reviews, technical proposals, and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Experience with container networking (CNI) and/or service mesh.

Job Description

Team Bio: 

ServiceNow’s Applied AI Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team is where bold ideas meet transformative action. We partner with our most strategic customers to shape the future of enterprise AI. Together, we identify high-value opportunities, accelerate business outcomes, and build reusable AI-native solutions that advance the Now AI Platform. 

Our mission: We partner deeply with our customers to build intelligent, scalable AI solutions that solve their most mission-critical challenges. By embedding in real-world complexity, we deliver fast, iterate with purpose, and transform every success into reusable patterns that accelerate transformation across the Now Platform and the broader enterprise. 

Why This Role Matters:

Enterprises are raising the bar. AI initiatives must deliver business value—not just promise potential. That means taking cutting-edge LLM capabilities and turning them into resilient, secure, and scalable software. 

As a Forward Deployed Solution Engineer (FDSE), you act as the CTO of the build—owning everything from backend services to LLM pipelines and front-end integrations. You partner with customers in the field to design, implement, and deliver solution-ready builds in agile sprints. Your software becomes the reference implementation for scalable GenAI in the enterprise. You codify patterns, shape internal tooling, and accelerate innovation—delivering systems that are battle-tested in production and scalable across industries. 

Who You Are:

You are a systems-minded, AI-native engineer who ships real software. You own the full stack—and are equally motivated by elegant APIs, intuitive UIs, and scalable orchestration pipelines. You think like a product-minded CTO, balancing creativity with pragmatism to deliver impact. 

You embed deeply with customer teams, diagnose root problems, and architect AI-powered workflows that run at scale. You don’t just debug code—you debug systems, context, and customer pain points. 

You will: 

  • Build solution-ready LLM-enabled applications that span backend logic, data orchestration, and front-end UI 
  • Operate in the field, working side-by-side with customers to adapt, deploy, and iterate in live environments 
  • Codify reusable assets—libraries, prompts, scaffolds—to accelerate future engagements 
  • Shape developer experience by sharing feedback with platform and product teams  

What You’ll Do: 

  • Deliver Production - readysolution in agile end-to-end sprints
  • Engineer with versatility: APIs, orchestration pipelines, vector DBs, LLM frameworks, UI components 
  • Operate with agility: integrate with legacy systems, navigate ambiguity, ship safely at speed 
  • Codify patterns: build scaffolds, SDKs, and documentation to scale success across customers 
  • Influence platform: inform product strategy through field-tested insights and extensible code 

What Success Looks Like:

  • Production-grade delivery: Your solution builds consistently convert to scaled deployments in production environments 
  • Reusable impact: You author libraries, prompts, and scaffolds that power multiple deployments and projects 
  • Platform influence: Your work shapes internal tooling and is integrated into platform roadmap and primitives 
  • Velocity and precision: You move fast without breaking things—shaping resilient, secure systems in high-stakes contexts 
  • Engineering leadership: You are trusted by architects, PMs, and customer teams to lead implementation from zero to one 

Qualifications

What You Bring:

  • Experience: In leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry
  • Relevant Experience: 10+ years of software engineering, including 2+ years building systems in customer-facing or embedded roles 
  • System architecture: Proven ability to design and implement AI-native software in production environments 
  • Engineering depth: Strength in backend (Python, Node.js, Java), frontend (React, Angular), APIs (REST/GraphQL) 
  • Machine Learning: Foundations of MLflow, Weights & Biases, LoRA, PEFT, SageMaker, Vertex AI, AzureML, Kubeflow, Airflow, Prefect, TorchServe, Triton, vLLM, SHAP, LIME, pandas, Spark, SQL
  • LLM tooling: Familiarity with LangChain, Semantic Kernel, prompt chaining, vector search, and context management 
  • Performance & observability: Skilled in debugging distributed systems, tuning for latency, and implementing monitoring 
  • Platform mindset: Can contribute to shared SDKs and tools, raising engineering velocity for the whole org 
  • Product sensibility: Prioritize for user value, MVP iteration, and long-term scale 
  • DevOps fluency: Experience deploying in AWS, Azure, or GCP with CI/CD, containers, and infra-as-code 
  • Field readiness: Able to travel up to 30% to embed onsite and deliver where it matters 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience integrating AI into SaaS platforms like ServiceNow or Salesforce 
  • Track record of production deployments in secure, regulated enterprise environments 
  • Contributions to dev experience tooling, frameworks, or reusable AI scaffolds

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

Position overview

A Regional Product Manager (RPM) connects global product strategy to execution in a specific market. Product managers build features and own the core roadmap with engineering teams. An RPM takes that roadmap into one market, adapts it to local customers, regulations, and buying patterns, and owns its commercial success there. At ServiceNow, RPM markets are defined by geography, industry, or customer segment.

In this role, you will own one industry or customer segment in the Americas. You will be the person responsible for how ServiceNow's AI products are positioned, sold, adopted, and improved in that market. This is an individual contributor (IC) role, reporting to the leader of Regional Product Management for the Americas.

Key Responsibilities

Regional strategy and adaptation

  • Translate the global AI product roadmap into a plan for your industry or segment 
  • Tailor use cases, solution packages, and messaging to the operational problems your customers care about most 
  • Account for industry regulations and compliance requirements in how solutions are positioned and deployed 
  • Track AI adoption trends in your market and adjust priorities as they shift 

Go-to-market and sales enablement

  • Partner with sales, marketing, and channel partners to launch AI products into your market 
  • Run discovery on priority deals and shape buying criteria and deal sizing toward AI early in the sales cycle 
  • Build discovery guides, use case catalogs, demo stories, and value stories that sellers can reuse 
  • Make sure AI use cases go live after every win, working with customer success, professional services, and partners on success criteria, go-live dates, and adoption metrics

Commercial strategy and financial targets

  • Own the commercial strategy for your market, including product mix, packaging, and deal structure, to meet revenue and margin targets 
  • Set and own quarterly targets for deals in motion, AI attach, and discovery completed before close 
  • Work with pricing teams on packaging and discount guidance suited to your customers 

Voice of the customer

  • Act as the technical and commercial expert in the field for your market 
  • Gather customer feedback and turn repeated needs into solution requirements for product teams 
  • Test emerging AI ideas with customers and bring the ones with traction to the teams that build new products 
  • Represent ServiceNow with customer executives, at industry events, and in customer advisory sessions 

Competitive intelligence

  • Monitor competitors selling AI into your market, including industry-specific vendors and horizontal AI platforms 
  • Analyze win/loss data to find patterns in why deals are won, lost, or stalled 
  • Equip sales teams with positioning and responses to competitor claims 

Qualifications

To excel as a Regional Product Manager (RPM), you need a unique blend of commercial acumen, cross-cultural leadership, and technical credibility. Because you sit between global development teams and local sales teams, your skillset must balance strategic thinking with ground-level execution.

Commercial and strategic skills

  • You design and run launch plans suited to how your market buys, including the partners, procurement processes, and executives involved 
  • You can set packaging and discount guidance and judge how deal structure affects margin 
  • You turn regulatory and compliance requirements into specific changes in how solutions are built, positioned, and deployed 

Relationship and communication skills

  • You align product teams and field sellers on priorities without direct authority over either 
  • You understand how business and IT leaders in your market make decisions, and you adjust how you communicate with each 
  • You manage expectations with senior product and sales leaders while supporting account teams on high-stakes customer deals 

Analytical and technical skills

  • You use sales data, win/loss results, and market share trends to decide where to focus 
  • You know enterprise AI and platform technology well enough to handle complex objections and train sellers 
  • You turn large volumes of customer feedback into a short, ranked list of requirements product teams can act on 

Experience

  • 10+ years in product management, solution consulting, or go-to-market strategy in enterprise software 
  • Domain depth in at least one industry or customer segment, including its core systems, regulations, and buyers 
  • A track record of influencing enterprise deals through discovery, solution design, or deal structure 
  • Experience taking AI or automation use cases from concept to production at customers 
  • Familiarity with the ServiceNow AI Platform (a plus)

title: Director, Solution Consulting - CRM Solutions
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

It all started in sunny San Diego, California in 2004 when a visionary engineer, Fred Luddy, saw the potential to transform how we work. Fast forward to today — ServiceNow stands as a global market leader, bringing innovative AI-enhanced technology to over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the Fortune 500®. Our intelligent cloud-based platform seamlessly connects people, systems, and processes to empower organizations to find smarter, faster, and better ways to work. But this is just the beginning of our journey. Join us as we pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone.

Why This Role Matters

You will lead one of  ServiceNow’s fastest-growing markets — and this team will be at the center of that momentum.

You’ll shape how we go to market, how we sell value, and how we build the next generation of Solution Consulting talent.

Job Description

As the Director, UKI CRM Solution Consulting, you run the day-to-day pre-sales engine for CRM across the UK, Ireland, and Scotland. You lead first-line Solution Consulting managers and their individual contributors, and you are the leader closest to the deals.

You know what each team is working on, what is landing with customers, and what is stalling. Your job is to remove the blockers, keep the team focused and motivated, and make sure Solution Consulting moves in step with its CRM selling peers. This is an execution role at heart: you make the engine go fast.

You report to the AVP, EMEA CRM Solution Consulting, who sets regional strategy and direction.

What you'll do...

Own the number -- deliver CRM NNACV for UKI

  • Carry accountability, with your first-line managers, for UKI CRM NNACV targets and contribute to the EMEA goal of double-digit ACV growth.
  • Forecast technical win rates and deal-by-deal readiness, and raise risk to the AVP early rather than late.
  • Work with UKI CRM sales leaders to focus Solution Consulting time on the opportunities, use cases, and industries where CRM wins fastest.

Know the deals on the ground

  • Maintain a detailed, current view of what each team is working on: active opportunities, technical stage, proof-of-value status, and next steps.
  • Know what is working and what is not, and act on it in the weekly deal and pipeline rhythms rather than in a quarterly review.
  • Join key customer, POV, and escalation discussions where technical credibility or senior air cover is needed.

Remove blockers and keep the team focused

  • Be the first escalation point for anything that slows a deal: environment access, resourcing conflicts, unclear scope, product gaps, or competing demands.
  • Protect the team's time by clearing distractions, cutting low-value requests, and making sure ICs spend their time on the deals that matter most.
  • Make sure every IC knows what good looks like on their deals and has what they need to deliver it.

Lead and develop first-line leaders and ICs

  • Coach first-line managers on deal reviews, technical strategy, and POV execution, and hold them to consistent motions and communication rhythms.
  • Recruit, develop, and retain strong technical talent, and build a bench of ready-now first-line leaders.
  • Give direct, regular feedback to ICs and managers, and address performance issues early.

Keep the team motivated and aligned to selling peers

  • Recognize wins visibly and often, and build a team rhythm that keeps morale and momentum high.
  • Run joint pipeline and deal reviews with CRM sales, value, partner, and product counterparts so Solution Consulting and selling teams operate as one engine.
  • Agree coverage, account plans, and proof strategy with the AEs before they reach the customer.

Drive the shift to POV-centric selling and the FDE model

  • Make working proof-of-value the default way the team earns technical trust, and help ICs move toward the Forward Deployed Engineer model of building alongside customers.
  • Use AI automation tools and standard POV frameworks to speed up demos, environment provisioning, and repeatable assets.

Connect the field to CRM product

  • Channel technical wins, losses, and product gaps from your team to the AVP and CRM product leaders, using specific, deal-level examples.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

  • 6+ years in a leadership role in Solution Consulting or a comparable pre-sales or technical sales function, including managing first-line leaders and individual contributors.
  • Still credible on the deals: you can scope a POV, work through an architecture question, or join a customer call without losing the thread.
  • A consistent record of owning and delivering against ACV / NNACV or equivalent revenue-tied targets in a software or SaaS environment.
  • Experience leading distributed teams across the UK, Ireland, and Scotland and operating effectively across cultures, languages, and time zones.
  • A working understanding of the CRM market and how AI and agentic automation are changing it.
  • Fluency with AI and automation tools and a bias toward using them to simplify how work gets done.
  • Experience moving a team from demo-centric to POV / proof-of-value-centric selling.
  • Clear, direct communication, and the ability to set a standard and hold first-line leaders to it.
  • Good operating judgement: knows when to escalate, when to decide, and when to get out of the way.
  • A talent-focused leader who can recruit, develop, and retain strong technical leaders and ICs.
  • Bachelor's degree in a technical or business field, or equivalent work experience.
  • Expected to travel up to 40% of the time on average, including across the UK, Ireland, and Scotland.

Job Description

ServiceNow is seeking a customer obsessed Senior Staff Outbound Product Manager to join the Data & Analytics product team responsible for Workflow Data Fabric and RaptorDB. This is an externally focused role for a product leader who can bring complex enterprise data capabilities to market through clear positioning, product launches, sales enablement, and direct customer engagement.

This role sits at the intersection of data architecture, platform performance, analytics, AI readiness, and customer value. You will help shape how ServiceNow customers understand, adopt, and unlock value from advanced data capabilities, translating deep technical concepts into compelling product narratives, go-to-market strategies, customer-facing content, and field enablement.

Business Context

Workflow Data Fabric and RaptorDB Professional are strategically important growth areas within ServiceNow’s Data & Analytics portfolio. The business is already significant, with approximately $600M in revenue and a goal to grow to $1.5B by 2029. The opportunity is not simply to sell data as a standalone product, but to build a clear wraparound strategy for how data enhances ServiceNow’s value proposition across workflows, customer outcomes, enterprise AI readiness, and strategic deal pursuits.

The right leader will identify the customer problem, craft the market narrative, and help scale field enablement and growth strategies through one-to-one, one-to-few, and one-to-many motions. This person will partner closely with product, engineering, sales, solution consulting, product marketing, and customer-facing teams to ensure the market understands the value of ServiceNow’s next-generation data platform.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the outbound product strategy for Workflow Data Fabric and RaptorDB Professional, translating complex data platform capabilities into clear customer value, differentiated positioning, and compelling market narratives.
  • Define and refine the core messaging, use cases, personas, competitive differentiation, and customer proof points that help technical and executive audiences understand why these products matter.
  • Partner closely with inbound product managers, engineering, product marketing, sales, solution consulting, and customer-facing teams to shape launch strategy, field readiness, growth motions, and adoption plans.
  • Serve as a product evangelist in customer briefings, executive conversations, analyst sessions, webinars, conferences, and strategic deal support, adapting the message for both technical practitioners and business decision-makers.
  • Translate concepts across enterprise data, analytics, integration, platform performance, and AI readiness into clear business outcomes, customer use cases, and seller-ready messaging without requiring audiences to navigate unnecessary technical depth.
  • Turn field feedback, customer insights, competitive intelligence, and adoption signals into actionable recommendations that influence roadmap priorities, GTM execution, and outbound investments.
  • Own high-impact outbound deliverables, including sales playbooks, product launch campaigns, demos, solution briefs, competitive guides, field training, executive presentations, and customer-facing product storytelling.
  • Help establish and track success metrics for outbound initiatives, including launch readiness, seller adoption, customer engagement, pipeline influence, product adoption, and market feedback.

title: Principal Software Engineer - Veza
descriptionHtml:
Company Description

Veza is the identity security platform for human, non-human, and AI agent access. Customers use it to see who and what has access to what, govern it, and remediate risk across cloud, SaaS, and on-prem systems.

Agent security is the inflection point. Static access reviews can't keep up with autonomous agents acting at machine speed. Security is shifting to continuous, real-time control: just-in-time access for agents, automated remediation of policy violations, and real-time governance of agent actions as they happen—replacing standing privileges and periodic reviews.

Veza is in transition, growing quickly as part of ServiceNow's Security & Risk organization. The Chief Architect will shape how the platform scales to meet this new category.

Job Description

What you'll do

Identity

  • Own the identity model for workloads and agents: SPIFFE/SPIRE trust domains, workload attestation, and how identities are issued, scoped, rotated, and revoked.
  • Architect ephemeral authentication and authorization end to end: short-lived credential issuance, token exchange and delegation (for example RFC 8693-style flows), and revocation that takes effect in practice.
  • Define runtime authorization for agents: what an agent can access, under whose delegated authority, with what guardrails, and with audit trails that hold up to review.
  • Lead the identity architecture for the Agent Security roadmap, including Runtime Authorization, the Access Policy Engine, and AgentID with short-lived credentials, and its integration with the NHI program.
  • Set the identity standards for non-human identities across Veza’s integrations, covering how connectors authenticate, get scoped, and rotate secrets.

Core architecture

  • Define identity contracts that the graph, data model, and integrations architects build against, and review designs in those areas for identity correctness.
  • Shape how identity fits into the Veza-ServiceNow integration model, including shared identity and data contracts and UI surfacing patterns.
  • Partner with the integrations, graph, and deployment owners on decisions that touch identity, without taking over their domains.

Leadership

  • Represent Veza’s identity architecture to customers, partners, ServiceNow Security leadership, and standards bodies.
  • Mentor engineers

Qualifications

What you bring

  • 12+ years in security or identity engineering, with a substantial share spent designing identity systems in production at scale.
  • Strong background in identity and access: IGA, IAM, PAM, authorization models, access reviews, lifecycle management, or adjacent security domains.
  • Deep hands-on expertise in workload identity, specifically SPIFFE/SPIRE or an equivalent, and in ephemeral credential design. You can explain trust bootstrapping and rotation failure modes without notes.
  • Strong grounding in OAuth 2.x, OIDC, token exchange, and authorization models (RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC, and policy engines such as OPA or Cedar).
  • Understanding of non-human identity (service accounts, secrets, API keys, workload identity) and emerging agent identity and authorization models.
  • Experience building security products that meet their own security and compliance bar (SOC 2, FedRAMP or equivalent, data residency).
  • Experience delivering production AI or agentic systems, including evaluation, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Active use of AI-native development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent).
  • Strong Python or Go, with the ability to go deep in code and design reviews.
  • Executive-level communication, with the ability to defend an identity decision to engineers, customers, and security leadership.
  • Breadth to hold your own on graph data models, integration architecture, and multi-region deployment, even if you don’t own them.
     

Preferred

  • Experience through an acquisition or platform integration, aligning an acquired architecture with a parent platform.
  • Experience with integration-heavy platforms and the authentication and secrets challenges they bring.
  • Familiarity with graph databases or immutable or event-sourced storage models.
  • Authored or shaped identity standards or RFCs.
  • Built or operated a production credential broker or identity provider.
  • BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Success in the first 12 months

  • A published identity architecture for workload and agent access, with committed milestones.
  • A defined, adopted model for ephemeral credentials across Veza’s services and integrations.
  • A runtime authorization design for agents that Product and Sales can take to customers.
  • Identity contracts agreed with the graph, integrations, and deployment owners.

Qualifications

descriptionHtml:
Company Description

ServiceNow is a global market leader in AI-enhanced cloud technology, serving over 8,100 customers, including 85% of the Fortune 500®. Our platform connects people, systems, and processes so organizations can work smarter, faster, and better. We pursue our purpose to make the world work better for everyone. 

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

As the AVP, AMS CRM Solution Consulting, you own the pre-sales technical engine behind one of ServiceNow's fastest-growing bets: CRM. You will lead a multi-layer organization of first- and second-line Solution Consulting leaders and their teams across the Americas, directly accountable for the Net New Annual Contract Value (NNACV) that CRM delivers. This is an execution role at heart. Your mandate is to convert ServiceNow's next-generation, AI-native CRM vision into consistent, repeatable pre-sales motions that win—at speed and at scale. 

You will re-establish a tight connection between the field and CRM product, build the next generation of pre-sales talent around the Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) model, and lead the shift from a demo-centric to a proof-of-value (POV) centric go-to-market motion. Above all, you will drive speed, simplification, and clarity—scaling the organization through AI automation and operating as a single, unified engine of execution alongside your CRM selling peers. 

What you'll do… 

Own the number – drive CRM NNACV growth 

  • Carry direct accountability for AMS CRM NNACV targets and mobilize the Solution Consulting organization to achieve and exceed double-digit ACV growth. 

  • Translate the number into clear team-level and individual pre-sales motions; forecast technical win rates and remove the blockers that slow deals. 

  • Partner with CRM sales leadership to prioritize the opportunities, use cases, and industries where CRM wins fastest. 

Build the next-generation pre-sales organization (FDE model) 

  • Lead and grow the next generation of pre-sales talent, evolving the Solution Consultant role toward the Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) model—technical leaders who build alongside customers rather than present to them. 

  • Participate in and accelerate the transition from a demo-centric to a POV-centric pre-sales GTM motion, making working proof-of-value the default way CRM earns technical trust. 

  • Recruit, develop, and retain elite technical talent, and build a bench of first- and second-line leaders ready for scale. 

Champion AI and the future of CRM

Scale through automation – speed, simplification, and clarity

  • Make speed, simplification, and clarity the operating standard for every motion the team runs. 

Reconnect the field to CRM product

  • Serve as a trusted voice of the customer, channeling technical wins, losses, and gaps into product priorities. 

  • Ensure the team consistently represents the current, differentiated CRM story—not the last generation's. 

Lead with consistent motions, clear messaging, and accountability 

  • Drive first- and second-line leaders to clear, consistent messaging and visible leadership accountability across the organization. 

  • Establish consistent motions and communication rhythms so every team runs the same plays to the same standard. 

  • Motivate the team and the broader CRM community to rally around shared, ambitious growth targets. 

Operate as a single engine of execution 

  • Work with CRM selling peers—sales, product, value, and partner leaders—as one integrated engine of execution, not adjacent functions. 

  • Align pre-sales strategy, coverage, and investment with the broader CRM go-to-market plan. 

  • Represent AMS CRM Solution Consulting in cross-functional and global forums, ensuring consistency across regions.

  • Extensive experience (10+ years) leading pre-sales, solution consulting, or technical sales organizations at scale, including leading other leaders (managing managers). This team is appox. 110 ICs and 16 managers.

  • A consistent record of owning and delivering against ACV / NNACV or equivalent revenue-tied targets in a software or SaaS environment.

As the Solution Architect for Public Sector India, you'll be the technical lead for ServiceNow's entry into the Indian public sector. You'll turn government digitisation programs into solution blueprints, proof of concepts, and winning bids, with AI at the centre of the story.

Purpose:

Design and deliver AI-led architectures aligned with the India AI Mission & ministry priorities, proof of concepts, and tender responses that win public sector business in India and build trust with government technology leaders and SI partners.

India Public Sector Context:

  • Design within government constraints: hosting, data localisation, security, AI governance, and integration with legacy and national platforms.
  • Co-sell with SIs and partners on solution scope, bid strategy, and delivery handoff.

Job Description

CEG AMS Partner Portfolio Excellence Lead 

Job Description 

The Role 

The CEG Americas (AMS) Partner Portfolio Excellence Lead owns the operational execution of the AMS partner portfolio and co-sell motion. The role aligns strategic partners to qualified account opportunities, converts AMS demand into actionable portfolio and capacity requirements, and helps ensure Partner commitments are deployed against the highest-value customer and business needs. 

Working across AMS sales, account, services, delivery, operations, GPC, and partner teams, the Senior Manager maintains a clear view of pipeline, allocation, utilization, and portfolio health. The role removes execution blockers, leads partner business reviews, and connects in-market demand with global portfolio governance so that partner investments translate into measurable pipeline, customer outcomes, and return. 

The role serves as the CEG geo interlock point for partner portfolio execution, connecting CEG demand, delivery fit, and partner capacity with GPC’s partner enablement and ecosystem readiness work while maintaining clear ownership boundaries between CEG delivery excellence and GPC partner capability-building. 

Responsibilities 

  • Own day-to-day execution of the AMS partner portfolio and co-sell motion, aligning strategic partners to qualified customer and account opportunities. 

  • Work with Services Sales Executives to build and maintain an integrated view of AMS partner-influenced pipeline, Partner allocations, committed capacity, utilization, delivery demand, and portfolio risks. 

  • Partner with AMS sales and account teams to identify partner-suitable opportunities, clarify partner value, and mobilize the right internal and partner stakeholders. 

  • Partner closely with GPC and geo partner sales teams to ensure partners have the enablement, capability signals, and ecosystem readiness needed to support CEG portfolio execution, while maintaining clear ownership boundaries between CEG delivery excellence and GPC partner enablement. 

  • Apply global commercial governance and account planning frameworks to AMS opportunities and partner relationships. 

  • Lead AMS partner business reviews, translating portfolio data into decisions, actions, owners, and follow-through rather than status reporting alone. 

  • Provide the AMS demand signal to Global Partner Portfolio Management so capacity and investment commitments are allocated where account and customer needs are strongest. 

  • Coordinate with Field Partner Operations to validate partner capacity, readiness, utilization, spend, forecast, onboarding status, and reporting accuracy. 

  • Coordinate with Partner Delivery leadership to check delivery capability, quality history, staffing readiness, and governance requirements before partner handoff, while leaving delivery readiness approval with the accountable Delivery Director. 

  • Remove commercial and operational blockers that slow partner co-sell execution, escalating material issues when required. 

  • Ensure portfolio decisions consider expected customer benefit, delivery fit, capability, and return on investment, not only available funding or capacity. 

  • Support joint account planning, partner opportunity reviews, pipeline inspections, and executive sponsorship for priority partner pursuits. 

  • Maintain clear portfolio documentation, decision logs, action tracking, and executive reporting for AMS leadership and global stakeholders. 

  • Identify opportunities to improve portfolio segmentation, opportunity routing, co-sell processes, analytics, and partner business review effectiveness. 

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience in partner portfolio management, co-sell execution, services sales operations, partner strategy, commercial operations, or a related role in a technology or SaaS environment. 

  • Experience working with account teams and partners to develop, qualify, advance, and govern partner-attached opportunities. 

  • Strong commercial and financial acumen, including pipeline management, investment allocation, capacity planning, forecasting, utilization, and return-on-investment analysis. 

  • Proven ability to synthesize portfolio data into clear recommendations, trade-offs, and executive decisions. 

  • Experience leading partner business reviews, account planning cadences, pipeline inspections, and cross-functional action tracking. 

  • Ability to coordinate across sales, delivery, operations, finance, customer success, GPC, and partner stakeholders to align portfolio execution with partner enablement and readiness activities in a matrixed environment. 

  • Strong understanding of the handoff between co-sell execution, contracting, capacity confirmation, delivery readiness, and post-sale governance. 

  • Excellent stakeholder management, communication, facilitation, and problem-solving skills. 

  • Demonstrated operational rigor, including maintaining accurate forecasts, portfolio records, decision logs, and follow-through on commitments. 

  • Knowledge of, or ability to rapidly develop proficiency in, ServiceNow’s platform, products, customer lifecycle, and partner ecosystem. 

  • Ability to operate across multiple AMS markets, balance competing priorities, and make progress through ambiguity. 

  • 6-8 years of relevant experience in partner management, sales operations, portfolio management, services strategy, or a related commercial role. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience with partner investment, capacity commitment, co-sell, or services funding models. 

  • Experience working with global systems integrators or other strategic technology and services partners. 

  • Familiarity with enterprise SaaS, professional services, customer success, adoption, and value realization motions. 

  • Experience building or scaling a partner pipeline, allocation, and portfolio performance management process. 

  • Advanced proficiency with CRM, pipeline analytics, forecasting, dashboarding, and executive reporting tools. 

  • Relevant certifications or formal training in finance, sales operations, partner management, program management, or analytics.

You will help shape what we build and take features from idea to production. We look for people who move fast, ask good questions, care about users, and take pride in their work.

Build a high-accountability, high-support team culture aligned to ServiceNow's values.

Determine territory design, industry vertical coverage (FSI, MRD, TMT, Public Sector), and partner selection criteria. Translate strategy into executable territory plans with each PSM and ensure quarterly execution discipline.

Elevate partner relationships at the leadership level, supporting your PSMs in building strong working relationships with selected partners' sales teams.
  • Demand generation and pipeline creation: Collaborate with the Partner Marketing Group to build and execute joint demand generation programmes across Asia's key verticals and partner ecosystem. Ensure pipeline creation targets are met through a balanced mix of partner-led events, digital campaigns, and direct prospecting with your team.
  • Executive engagement and deal support: Engage directly with C-suite and senior buyer stakeholders on strategic opportunities both to advance deals and to model the right level of executive engagement for your PSMs. Support the team in navigating complex, multi-stakeholder deal cycles with partner and internal pre-sales resources.
  • Asia market and industry expertise: Bring credible knowledge of Asia's enterprise technology landscape across key verticals FSI, MRD, TMT, and Public Sector. Understand the competitive dynamics, procurement patterns, partner ecosystem maturity, and digital transformation priorities specific to Asia's commercial market.
  • Reporting and business rhythm: Establish and maintain a regular operating cadence of weekly pipeline reviews, monthly business reviews, and quarterly planning sessions with your team, partners, and APAC leadership. Provide clear, data-driven reporting on team performance, pipeline health, and market trends.

  • Channel and partner sales: Deep experience building and executing partner-led sales motions by co-selling with partners, managing partner-influenced pipeline, and driving partner accountability for revenue outcomes. Knows the difference between managing partners and selling through them.
  • Asia enterprise market expertise: Strong understanding of Asia's enterprise technology landscape including major buying centres, procurement dynamics, key partner ecosystems (SIs, VARs, GSIs with Asia presence), and the competitive SaaS environment. Local network is a significant advantage.
  • Industry vertical knowledge: Working knowledge across Asia's priority verticals: Financial Services (FSI), Manufacturing / Retail & Distribution (MRD), Technology / Media / Telecom (TMT), and Public Sector. Able to coach PSMs on vertical-specific positioning and to engage credibly with senior industry buyers.
  • Enterprise SaaS platform fluency: Familiarity with enterprise SaaS platforms, ideally ServiceNow, Salesforce, SAP, or comparable workflow / ITSM / ERP solutions. Able to position platform value at business and IT decision-maker level and coach reps to do the same.

  • CSA certificate
  • 5+ years of Channel/partnerships Sales

  • 5+ ServiceNow platform or technical expertise with cloud software solutions
  • Experience working collaboratively with product management, product marketing, partners, and professional services

  • Travel, as required.

Job Description

The Role  

As the Global Technology Enablement Manager, you will serve as a cross-functional technology generalist within the Enablement organization, bridging the gap between engineering, product, and technical field roles. You understand what it takes to deliver impactful live customer demos—while also possessing the deep technical capability to build, scale, and maintain hands-on lab environments.  

This role centers on core technical execution, demo craftsmanship, and practical hands-on learning environments. You will support a diverse set of technical audiences—including Pre-Sales Solution Consultants, Post-Sales Delivery Assurance teams, and Strategic Partners. You will act as the technical voice across these teams, owning the execution of pre-configured demo and sandbox instances, refining Proof-of-Value (POV) frameworks, and coaching engineers on how to demonstrate real-world solution value.  

This is a highly hands-on role. You won’t just design enablement strategies—you will build lab guides, automate environment deployments, score live demo evaluations, and ensure our entire technical field ecosystem is equipped to win.  

Qualifications

What You’ll Do

  • Demo & Lab Ecosystem Ownership: Design, scale, and maintain secure, pre-configured "seeded" environments and customizable testing instances used across Pre-Sales demos, Post-Sales Delivery Assurance validations, and Partner hands-on labs.  

  • Core Sales Skills & Demo Coaching: Train Solution Consultants and technical field teams on demo delivery best practices, value-based storytelling, and effective objection handling during live customer interactions.  

  • Cross-Functional Environment Advocacy: Serve as the technical bridge to Product Development and Engineering, translating field needs into actionable requirements for live demo instances, sandbox automation, and release readiness.  

  • POV & Post-Sales Execution Frameworks: Develop repeatable technical playbooks, architectural lab guides, and Proof of Value (POV) methodologies to accelerate both deal conversion and post-sales time-to-value.  

  • Competency Validation & Train-the-Trainer: Build practical proof-of-knowledge evaluations (e.g., live demo scoring, hands-on lab validations), and deliver "train-the-trainer" sessions to scale enablement across internal and external partners.  

  • Technical Content Engineering: Write, update, and maintain comprehensive, repeatable lab guides, architecture playbooks, and video modules using tools like Articulate Rise and Camtasia.  

What You Bring 

  • Field-Tested Solution Consultant Experience: Direct, hands-on experience carrying a bag as a Solution Engineer, Pre-Sales Consultant, or Systems Engineer. You have delivered live customer demos, run technical POVs, and navigated complex technical evaluations. 

  • Cybersecurity & Technical Generalist Expertise: Strong foundation across enterprise cybersecurity domains (e.g., asset management, CTEM, threat detection, cloud security) paired with broad systems administration knowledge (virtualization, cloud infrastructure). 

  • Lab Infrastructure & Automation Skills: Experience building or scripting demo/lab environments using automation tools (e.g., Terraform, Ansible, or cloud-native templates) to spin up, refresh, and maintain reliable test instances. 

  • Multi-Audience Versatility: Ability to effectively engage and enable varied technical personas—from Pre-Sales SCs and Post-Sales Delivery Assurance Engineers to external Partner Architects. 

  • "How to Show Value" Coaching: Track record of coaching technical professionals on presentation skills, demo craftsmanship, and practical execution, rather than relying on product-only slides. 

  • Tooling Proficiency: Familiarity with instructional design/authoring tools (Articulate Rise, Camtasia), LMS platforms, and lab/environment management tools.
